answer.rationale: Write p99 went 5x starting ~30 minutes after a release, during a daily settlement peak that is normally handled. That points to a change-induced write-path regression more than a routine capacity miss. Writes are primary-affine, so confinement to the primary region does not by itself diagnose a regional infra failure. Failover or a payments circuit breaker during peak settlement would risk dropping or splitting customer writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing addresses report/read load, not heavy writes. memory_b1 is the closest successful write-preserving recovery; memory_b6 says release regressions surface within about an hour, which matches this timeline. Symptom mismatch remains (b1 was an error spike, not latency), so b1 is the one record to reopen. Uncertainty that this is load-only rather than the build is still open.
